samples.summary: Published CLI docs left out of step: no `folders` namespace, no `docs copy` / `docs move`
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:120-134 enumerates the command tree (`docs`, `sheets`, `slides`, `notes`, `files`, `api-keys`, utilities) and :141-163 lists the `docs` subcommands (list/create/get/rename/delete). The diff adds a whole new top-level `folders` namespace (packages/cli/src/cli.ts registerFoldersCommand) plus `docs copy` and `docs move` (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:169-216), none of which appear in the shipped user docs. Nothing enforces this (no docs-coverage test exists in packages/documentation), so the drift ships silently. Fix belongs in the documentation package, not in the new code.
searchedFor: Grep 'registry|getCommandSchema' across repo for a docs/registry parity check

samples.summary: Public REST reference documents neither the new `/folders` endpoints nor `POST /documents/:did/copy`, and still implies an unrestricted PATCH/DELETE for API keys
samples.evidence: packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:96-120 documents Get/Update/Delete Document with no mention of the manager-only rule the diff now enforces for API keys (documents.controller.ts:158-184), no `folderId` field on PATCH, no `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/documents/:did/copy`, and no Folders section at all. The internal design doc (docs/design/rest-api.md:499-534) was updated; the published one was not.

samples.summary: Agent skill files (the CLI's own machine-facing docs) never mention `docs copy`, `docs move`, or the folders namespace
samples.evidence: packages/cli/skills/docs-manage.md contains no match for 'folder', 'move' or 'copy', and packages/cli/skills/SKILL.md's skill index (line 49 area) lists files/sheets/slides/docs skills with no folders entry. These files are the discovery surface agents read to learn what the CLI can do, so a new namespace that is absent from them is effectively unreachable for that consumer. No lane checks skill/registry parity.
searchedFor: Grep 'skills' across packages/cli for a parity test

samples.summary: Every API-key request to /api/v1 now costs two extra queries; the workspace id is resolved twice per request
samples.evidence: WorkspaceScopeGuard already calls `resolveId(workspaceId)` (workspace-scope.guard.ts:37) and now also calls `assertMember(resolvedId, …)`, whose first statement is another `resolveId` (workspace.service.ts:236-243) followed by the member lookup. Previously the API-key path short-circuited before either. Same double-resolve now happens in image-read.controller.ts:108 on a route throttled at 600 req/min that serves every embedded image. Behaviourally correct, just an unnoticed per-request cost on the hottest v1 paths; `assertMember` could take the already-resolved id or the guard could skip the second resolve.

samples.summary: Existing API-key integrations that delete documents authored by other members will start receiving 403 with no migration note anywhere outside the design doc
samples.evidence: `remove` used to skip the manager check entirely for API keys (old comment: 'API keys ... act with workspace authority'); it now requires `isDocumentManager(member.role, doc.authorID, userId)` for keys too. The only in-repo caller is the CLI (`packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:308 deleteDocument`, surfaced as `docs delete`), whose docs (packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:161) still present delete as unconditional. Impact is bounded because keys are mintable only by owners (`assertOwner`) and an owner is always a manager, but any deployment where a minter's role or membership changed out of band silently loses delete/move across the whole key. No release note or user-facing doc records the new failure mode.
searchedFor: Grep 'apiKey.create|api-keys' repo-wide for keys minted outside ApiKeyService
